items.title: Movement seeks $1.2M clawback: Vet signing bonus terms now
items.description: Movement seeks $1.2M clawback: Vet signing bonus terms now By Andrew Martinez CloseText About Andrew twitter andrewomartinez mailto andrew.martinez@arizent.com linkedin andrewomartinez Published November 10, 2026, 6:00 a.m. EST | Updated November 10, 2026, 10:52 a.m. EST 2 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Key Insight: Learn why Movement Mortgage is demanding over $1 million back from two fired originators. Supporting data: Fifteen percent of the lender's producing workforce departed the company in 2023. Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. One of the nation's largest lenders wants over $1 million back from two originators it fired after rates shot up earlier this decade. Movement Mortgage filed a petition in federal court this week to confirm an arbitration award of at least $1,235,000 against two Chicago-based employees. While clawback requests have persisted since the massive layoff rounds earlier this decade, the Movement filing is one of the largest individual amounts sought by a lender in recent years. Processing Content Victor Shkolnikov and Igor Velyunskiy were paid $835,000 and $400,000, respectively, in early 2022 to operate a Chicago branch, according to case filings. They were terminated a year later, after their production fell precipitously alongside a major rise in mortgage rates. The pair filed counterclaims against Movement, but an arbitrator denied their arguments in a hearing this summer. Shkolnikov and Velyunskiy now face a payment potentially exacerbated by 8% statutory interest accruing since their April 2023 firing, according to Movement. Both originators remain in the industry. They did not comment, while neither Movement nor its attorney responded to requests for comment. Poor performance in a worsening market Lengthy filings describe Shkolnikov and Velyunskiy's employment agreements and performance, with the lender claiming they lost money every month. The company says the originators ended their run with a negative $459,928 profit share, and cost Movement $350,281 on the Chicago branch. According to the filing, the pair averaged $36 million per month in origination volume before joining, but just around $4 million per month once joining Movement. Modex data shows the originators' production fell significantly once joining Movement, with only a few units per month toward the end of 2022. From around the time of the duo's hiring, the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up from around 4% in March 2022 to the low-to-mid 6% range in April 2023. In the arbitration proceedings, the originators filed counterclaims over the terms of their employment agreement, including purported Regulation Z and wage law violations regarding their compensation. An arbitrator denied all of their claims, citing their employment agreement's at-will language, and because of a lack of evidence presented at the hearing. "HELOCs let them borrow against their equity without giving up the low interest rate on their home," said certified financial planner Douglas Boneparth, president and founder of Bone Fide Wealth in New York City and a member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council . Mortgage holders have $17.5 trillion in equity Mortgage holders collectively had $17.5 trillion in home equity as of the third quarter, according to a new report from Intercontinental Exchange, a financial markets technology and data company. Tappable equity that can be accessed — meaning a homeowner's equity would remain at or above 20% of the home's value after tapping it — rose 1.2%, or $16,600, from a year ago to an average of $204,000 per borrower, the ICE report shows. "Homeowners are sitting on substantial housing wealth, with 2.4 million mortgage holders now holding at least $1 million in equity," Andy Walden, head of mortgage and Housing Market Research at ICE, said in the report. Average HELOC rate is 7.49% HELOCs let you tap a line of credit over time as you need the money, instead of getting it all at once like a home equity loan or cash-out refinance. While HELOCs may have fewer upfront costs than a home equity loan, they generally have a variable interest rate. This means it will move up and down based on a benchmark like the prime rate, which banks use as a basis to set rates on a variety of loans. And, while the Federal Reserve doesn't control that rate, it is influenced by changes the Fed makes to the so-called federal funds rate. "If your budget only works at today's rate, then your budget doesn't really work," Boneparth said of HELOCs. "You kind of have to be mindful of the fact that rates may go up." During that time, you typically are only required to pay the interest on any funds you've withdrawn. After that, however, you'll enter a repayment period of, say, 10 or 20 years, when you're required to pay both interest and principal. Because of that, your payments will jump if you've only been paying interest. "The real test comes when the repayment period kicks in, and the principal starts to show up, if that's how their HELOC is structured," Boneparth said. items.title: ‘Landman’ Season 3 Is Filming at Taylor Sheridan’s 600-Acre Texas Ranch—Which He Previously Charged Paramount $50K a Week To Use
items.description: Actor and director Taylor Sheridan has created an impressive slate of ranch-themed TV shows , but what is perhaps more remarkable is that some of them have been filmed on his very own properties. The “ Yellowstone ” creator, 56, boasts an extraordinary property empire that’s estimated to be worth more than $600 million. And one of his most recognizable properties—the 600-acre Bosque Ranch near Fort Worth, TX —will reportedly be a filming location in Season 3 of the Sheridan-produced show “Landman.” One of the series’ cast members, musician Clayton Q , confirmed the plans in a Nov. 6 Instagram post . “Hey, y’all, Clayton Q here. I’m here at the world-famous Bosque Ranch right here in Weatherford, TX ,” he said in the video. “Taylor Sheridan’s horse ranch. We got a lot of stuff going on. I’m on location today.” Season 3 of the series began filming in October and is expected to premiere in mid-2027. It comes at a slight delay, as the season was green-lit in December 2025. Loading... Taylor Sheridan, the creator of shows such as "Yellowstone," "Landman," and "Lioness," has an impressive portfolio of properties worth nearly $600 million. Getty Images for SiriusXM Loading... His primary residence, Bosque Ranch in Texas, is being used as a filming location for Season 3 of "Landman." YouTube/Bosque Ranch The Bosque Ranch Headquarters website confirms the legendary spot has been used to film a handful of projects, including “Yellowstone,” “Lawman: Bass Reeves,” and “Lioness.” According to the Wall Street Journal , Sheridan had reportedly charged Paramount $50,000 a week to film at the ranch. His cattle was rented in herds, priced at $25 a cow. Sheridan snapped up the property in 2013 for a whopping $264 million. At the time, the ranch served as a home base for his family, who had relocated to the Lone Star State from Los Angeles , where he previously worked as an actor on shows such as “Veronica Mars” and “Sons of Anarchy.” Today, the home remains Sheridan’s primary residence, although he and his wife, actress-model Nicole Muirbrook , also spend time with their son at another property they own in Texas —the Four Sixes Ranch he purchased for $320 million in 2022. “The main headquarters where we live is more of a horse ranch, because I’m pretty deep into the horse deal. And then the ranch out by Jacksboro is more where we run the cattle,” he explained in a 2020 interview . Loading... While Sheridan and his wife, Nicole Muirbrook, own multiple homes, they spend the most of their time at the 600-acre Bosque Ranch. Instagram/Nicole Muirbrook Sheridan Sheridan also has a $4.95 million ranch in Wyoming’s Star Valley, which he reportedly acquired in August 2024 . The 179-acre homestead is known as Papa’s Creek Ranch and is located about 65 miles from Jackson Hole . Despite his jaw-dropping portfolio, Sheridan hasn’t always been well-off financially. In an August 2026 interview with Town and Country magazine , he recalled a time when he was down on his luck. “I was homeless twice,” he said. “I lived in my car. Sometimes I’d go to Ojai , just somewhere where I could safely sleep. I did that for six months.” The multihyphenate noted that the struggle was technically his own choice. “I could have decided at any point, ‘I’m going to get a full-time job and I’m going to give up this dream,’” he said of his acting career. “And I chose to sleep in my car over that.” However, when he became more successful, after his stint on “Sons of Anarchy,” he developed a strategy to make sure he could solidly stand on his own two feet from there on out. After turning to screenwriting, he sold his first screenplay for a drama called “Hell or High Water.” Afterward, he “bought a little house on an acre on a river in Wyoming.” “We moved there, and I wrote a check for it,” he said. “Then, as I would start to have more success, I would buy a little bit more land beside it and get a couple horses. I’m still so averse to having to ever owe anybody anything.” Sheridan explained that now that he’s built a career tied so deeply to ranching, he can avoid Los Angeles, a city he disliked living in. “I don’t leave the ranch,” he said. items.title: Ring Drone Cam Becomes a Reality for Homeowners Eager To Level Up With Smart Home Security
items.description: If you remember Rosie from “The Jetsons,” congratulations—the future is here. Amazon’s Ring announced the launch of two new products on Tuesday, offering homeowners room-to-room surveillance and smart home functionality in brand-new ways. First, there’s an indoor security drone. The Ring Drone Cam is a security camera that takes flight in your home, including upstairs, to monitor your house activity, day and night. At a demonstration in New York on Monday, Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff showed how the drone could be used as a home monitoring tool and as a crime “deterrent.” “If someone is going around your house at night, and your motion detector goes off on your Ring doorbell, imagine if you see spotlights and something flying across the window,” Siminoff said, according to CNBC . “You’re probably not going to go into that house.” Secondly, there is the Ring Rover Cam. Seen by most as an upgrade to Amazon’s 2021 Astro home robot, this free-roaming bot is being pushed more for companies to patrol offices, warehouses, and other workspaces. But it is a clear indication of where the technology for your home may head next. Loading... Home security takes flight with the Ring Drone Cam, which can cruise your entire house, including upstairs. Ring Loading... Instant mapping allows the drone to learn every inch of your home Ring Smart home technology reaching new heights The Ring Drone is being touted as a product meeting the moment of consumers eager to keep their most powerful asset protected at every level. “For years, customers told us they wanted eyes in the places a fixed camera couldn’t reach, and peace of mind in the spots they’d never want one,” said Siminoff in the company’s press release . “The honest answer wasn’t more cameras; it meant reimagining what a security device could be. That kind of invention is hard, and it takes time. But we kept at it until we got it right—and that's Ring Robotics. It’s not just a new category of security; it’s the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have.” Priced at $250, the Ring Drone flying indoor security camera is a first-of-its-kind Ring camera, “built from the ground up with AI at its core,” according to the company. Spec and key features include the following: Custom flight routes: Homeowners can set routes and a schedule, and Ring Drone flies them automatically. You can also deploy it on demand, as the promo video shows. Automatic incident response: When a Ring camera, sensor, or alarm is triggered, Ring Drone automatically flies to previously set patrol points to investigate. Wall-to-wall coverage: With a 148-degree field of view and the ability to rotate 360 degrees, Ring Drone provides a whole-room view in 2K video. Captures video day or night: Two built-in LED lights activate automatically in low-light environments, so you always get clear, crisp video. Seamless Ring integration: Works with Ring cameras, doorbells, sensors, and alarms out of the box, and can be controlled from the newly updated Alexa Home Map . Loading... The drone paired with the new Rover Ring Loading... You can autonomously patrol your business, send to preset viewpoints, and scan areas of interest. Ring A Rover Boy The Ring Drone was announced as part of the launch of Ring Robotics, which takes everything “customers already love and trust about Ring and puts it in motion,” according to the company announcement. While the Ring Drone is presented as a home product, the company’s debut of Ring Rover is designed for business. An autonomous security robot, the $1,000 device is designed to give a roving security to offices, warehouses, and other larger footprint facilities. Admittedly, the company created the Ring Rover after receiving feedback from Amazon Astro customers who said the feature they loved seeing is security on the move. “As leaders in home and business security, the Ring team took that feedback, leveraged the best of Astro, and built something new—not a home robot that also does security, but a purpose-built security robot,” reads the press release. Key features and capabilities of Ring Rover include the following: Full-spectrum scanning: The Ring Rover can travel to any saved checkpoint or room with one tap. It can then execute a complete 360-degree scan to ensure total coverage. Customizable patrol schedules: Set automated monitoring routes that fit your business schedule, allowing Ring Rover to patrol off-hours when a workspace is empty. Automated event investigation: Triggers from connected Ring devices prompt Ring Rover to autonomously navigate to designated patrol points to assess the situation. Height-adjustable periscope camera: An extendable mast allows the camera to see above shelving, counters, and obstacles. Height settings can be customized and saved for specific stops. Visible and audible deterrents: Equipped with an integrated siren, light tower, and two-way audio, Ring Rover signals an active security presence and enables direct real-time communication. Continuous 4K video recording: Streams and records up to 4K video during motion and patrols, capturing footage along the entire route for later review.* The Ring Drone Cam ships in the U.S. on Jan. 27, pending approval from the Federal Communications Commission, while the Ring Rover Cam will begin shipping to users on Dec. 16, the company said. items.description: A potential nor’easter impacting the Northeast and New England is being forecasted for later this week, with millions of homeowners bracing for possibly the first snow of the season. Meteorologists are predicting that as early as Wednesday evening, a deep plunge in temperatures combined with a low pressure system moving across the Midwest will make for wet conditions for Louisville, KY , all the way up to Maine . While snow in these areas this time of year is not unheard of, some locales are prepping for a volatile winter ahead, given the Super El Niño conditions. So is this just a taste of what’s to come? A nor’easter in November Cold air sweeps across the East late in the week, setting the stage for winter weather, according to The Weather Channel . By Thursday night, a secondary low-pressure system is expected to form off the Eastern Seaboard. As cold air filters in, rain could begin mixing with or fully changing over to wet snow across interior parts of the Northeast. Friday into the weekend presents the greatest potential for snow, depending on the storm’s exact track, which meteorologists are still unclear on. If the system tracks close to the coast, it could wrap heavy inland snowfall into the Northeast alongside coastal rain, strong winds, and flooding. A track farther out to sea would result in much lighter snow accumulations across inland areas. Homeowners in places like Buffalo, NY , and Burlington, VT , are among those who should prepare for the snow shovels and salt for a snowy weekend. However, if the temperatures dip low enough, it wouldn’t be unthinkable to see snow in places like Washington, DC, Philadelphia, and New York City as well. Loading... Cold air will settle in for millions across the East as a storm could bring rain, snow, and winds to the Northeast. The Weather Channel Prepping for the winter Speaking of New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced ahead of the nor’easter a citywide mobilization to prepare Manhattan for winter weather. This includes a $25 million investment in an expanded Code Blue system and a supercharged snow- and ice-clearing operation. “We have spent the past year preparing for any challenge winter throws our way. We have trained our workers, readied our equipment and strengthened our protocols because keeping New Yorkers safe can’t begin when the first storm hits,” Mamdani said in a press release. “This winter, we’re doing things differently—we’re expanding Code Blue to reach more New Yorkers in need, equipping New York’s Strongest to clear snow and ice faster and leaving no stone unturned when it comes to protecting our neighbors from the cold. No New Yorker should face the dangers of winter alone, and no part of our city should be left behind.” These initiatives come at a time where New York and much of the surrounding states are bracing themselves for the final months of the Super El Nino, which, according to the latest forecasts from the World Meteorological Organization, is projected to be the strongest on record and likely to persist through February 2027. According to the NOAA , an El Niño system tends to be strongest during the winter months. But because of the strength of the system being tracked this year, there are plenty of variables at play. “Every El Niño is not the same; each one is unique with its own imprint on our weather,” says Ken Graham , director of NOAA’s National Weather Service (NWS). "Advanced monitoring and an improved understanding of El Niño patterns allow the NWS to better predict and better prepare the public and our core partners for what is to come.” With that in mind, the Farmers' Almanac 2026–'27 winter outlook outlines a season defined by sharp contrasts and volatile conditions across the United States, driven largely by an active El Niño pattern. In the Northeast, it predicts a season dominated by wet conditions, both rainy and snowy. In fact, much of the country will need to contend with wetter than usual conditions, but whether snow develops will depend largely on the temperatures. items.title: Housing Finance at a Glance: A Monthly Chartbook, October 2026
items.description: Housing Finance at a Glance is a monthly reference guide for mortgage and housing market data. It includes more than 80 curated and updated figures describing current trends in the US housing finance market, including housing affordability, credit availability, serious delinquency rates, and mortgage insurance activity. The following trends from this edition stood out most to housing finance policy researchers: Aggregate households’ equity is $35.8 trillion (page 6). Higher interest rates are pulling back refinancing. Mortgage rates have increased from a 2026 low of 5.98 percent in February to 7.24 percent in October (page 9). As a result, the share of agency mortgages that are refinanceable has fallen from 11.5 percent to just 2.0 percent (page 10). The cash-out refinance share of all refinancings has increased, but the refinance volume remains low (page 12). The share of loans in negative or near-negative equity sits at 2.75 percent (page 29). Rising rates are also slowing production: Fannie Mae and the Mortgage Bankers Association project quarterly originations to fall from $550 to $570 billion in Q1 2026 to $450 to $460 billion in Q4 (page 21). Housing starts are forecasted to decrease to 1.25 to 1.30 million in 2027 (page 22), and government-sponsored enterprise net issuance has turned negative (-$39.2 billion year to date) (page 35). items.title: Cushman & Wakefield Announces Sale of Historic 121 W. Wacker to Chicago-Based Investor Group
items.description: Cushman & Wakefield Announces Sale of Historic 121 W. Wacker to Chicago-Based Investor Group Jeremy Barewin • 11/10/2026 Cushman & Wakefield Retained as Exclusive Leasing Agent 121 W. Wacker, Chicago CHICAGO -- Cushman & Wakefield (NYSE: CWK), a leading global real estate services firm, today announced the sale of 121 W. Wacker, a landmark 41-story office tower overlooking the Chicago River and located at the gateway to Chicago's historic LaSalle Street corridor. The 441,030-square-foot property was acquired by two Chicago-based investors Ken Buckman and Robert Castillo, who intend to invest substantial capital to re-energize the nearly century-old building. Cushman & Wakefield's Cody Hundertmark and Tom Sitz represented the seller, Chicago-based real estate firm Ameritus, in the transaction. Following the acquisition, Cushman & Wakefield has been retained as the exclusive leasing agent for the property, with Mason Taylor and Paige Krueger leading leasing efforts. Unlike many institutional office investors, the principals come from business entrepreneurship and private equity. Their vision for the property's next chapter centers on long-term ownership, thoughtful modernization and renewing its prominence as one of downtown Chicago's enduring architectural landmarks. "Owning 121 W. Wacker is about much more than acquiring a real estate asset," said Buckman. "As Chicago residents, we felt strongly that 121 W. Wacker should remain in local hands. The property has a remarkable history, an irreplaceable location and a presence in the Chicago skyline that deserves thoughtful stewardship. We have ambitious plans to modernize the tenant experience while preserving the character and architectural details that make this one of the city's great buildings." The ownership group is planning a series of capital improvements to position the tower for the needs of today's leading companies. Enhancements include a significant upgrade to the outdoor amenity terrace and 24th floor conference center, a completely remodeled restaurant and bar managed by a leading Chicago hospitality firm and a refreshed main lobby experience. Award-winning international design firm Ware Malcomb will oversee all interior and exterior architecture, with Ameritus continuing as the building's property manager. Situated at the intersection of Wacker Drive and LaSalle Street, the property offers sweeping views of the Chicago River and skyline, immediate access to the Chicago Riverwalk and multiple public transportation options. The location places it amid the growing residential and business activity reshaping the Loop, just one block from Google's new Chicago headquarters, scheduled to open next year. "121 W. Wacker remains one of the most distinctive office buildings in downtown Chicago, offering something that cannot be replicated: authentic architectural character in an unmatched riverfront location," said Mason Taylor, Executive Managing Director, Agency Leasing at Cushman & Wakefield. "The new ownership group brings an entrepreneurial mindset, a genuine commitment to Chicago and a willingness to invest in the building's future. With planned upgrades throughout the property, it is exceptionally well-positioned to attract companies seeking a premier office environment, centrally located along Wacker Drive." Completed in 1930 and designed by renowned Chicago architects Holabird & Root, 121 W. Wacker stands as one of the city's most recognizable Art Deco skyscrapers. Originally known as the LaSalle-Wacker Building, the tower helped establish the northern gateway to Chicago's historic financial district and was among the last major buildings constructed in the city before the Great Depression. Now included within the West Loop-LaSalle Street Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places, the building has witnessed nearly a century of Chicago's evolution, with early ties to two iconic companies, United Airlines and McDonald's, both of which once maintained offices at the property. items.description: Cushman & Wakefield Brokers $44 Million Sale of 240-Unit Apartment Community in Sheboygan, Wisconsin to Axiom Properties Jeremy Barewin • 11/9/2026 The Corridor garnered significant investor interest, attracting more than 25 offers The Corridor SHEBOYGAN, WISC. -- Cushman & Wakefield (NYSE: CWK), a leading global real estate services firm, today announced that its Multifamily Advisory Group has brokered the $44 million sale of The Corridor, a 240-unit Class A multifamily community in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, to Axiom Properties. Cushman & Wakefield's Brad Smith, Jack Maloney and Ralph Depasquale represented the seller, Chicago-based Midloch Investment Partners. Located at 1436 Green Street, the community was approximately 97% occupied at the time of sale. Under the seller's ownership, occupancy increased by nearly 25 percentage points in roughly 13 months. The sale also includes an in-place tax increment financing (TIF) agreement, which reimburses 65% of the incremental property tax through 2038 and enhances cash flow for the new owner. The Corridor benefits from a location within 30 minutes of more than 60,000 jobs, including major regional employers such as Kohler, Aurora Health Care, Sargento and Rockline Industries. Within a five-mile radius of the property, apartment occupancy exceeds 97%, while the area has seen no new multifamily deliveries since 2024 despite a sizeable population of renter households earning $50,000 or more annually. "Tertiary Midwest markets supported by strong employment fundamentals and limited new supply are attracting significant investor interest," said Smith, Managing Director, Cushman & Wakefield. "We received 25 offers from institutional, national, regional and private buyers, underscoring the depth of demand for stable, insulated markets like Sheboygan. As one of the largest multifamily transactions in the market in recent years, The Corridor presented a rare opportunity to acquire a high-quality asset with both strong in-place performance, cash flow stability and future upside." Completed in 2021 on a 13.44-acre site, The Corridor features one-, two- and three-bedroom residences across three residential buildings, along with a fitness center, resident lounge, community room, dog park, playground, outdoor gathering spaces and parking. Apartment homes feature granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, luxury vinyl plank flooring, in-unit washers and dryers, and select private balconies. Residents also enjoy convenient access to downtown Sheboygan, Lake Michigan beaches, retail destinations and recreational amenities. items.title: The Next Dollar: How Generational Spending Shifts Are Reshaping Retail Real Estate
items.description: The Next Dollar: How Generational Spending Shifts Are Reshaping Retail Real Estate Nov 10, 2026 U.S. Retail Research Report The next generation of retail growth is taking shape. Download Report Authors Nicole Larson Senior Manager, National Retail Research | U.S. Anjee Solanki National Director, Retail Services & Practice Groups The next generation of retail growth is taking shape. Who will drive the next dollar of retail spending, and what will it mean for physical stores? Colliers' latest retail report, The Next Dollar, explores how shifting consumer spending power, shopping behaviors and generational preferences are reshaping the retail landscape through 2030. While millennials will remain the largest consumer spending group, Gen Z is emerging as a major force in retail growth. At the same time, physical stores continue to play an essential role across all six generations, serving different needs for discovery, convenience, service and connection. Inside the report: A new generation of spending power: Gen Z spending is projected to grow 85.6% to $1.61 trillion by 2030, while Millennials retain the largest share of retail spending. The enduring value of physical retail: Every generation is expected to make the majority of its retail purchases in stores through 2030, reinforcing the importance of the physical shopping experience. The categories capturing growth: Foodservice, apparel and beauty are among the fastest-growing retail categories, creating opportunities for evolving tenant mixes and cross-shopping. The influence of tomorrow's consumers: Gen Z is driving demand for wellness, discovery and real-world connection, while Gen Alpha is already influencing household purchasing decisions. For retailers, property owners and investors, understanding these generational shifts will be critical to creating destinations that remain relevant as consumer expectations evolve.
